issues.reason: *Quantifiers, generics & scope* makes the per-member rule the mandated form for a distributive predicate over a grouped plural - "the dogs barked" is its own cited example - and *Negation (events)* confirms the positive sentence emits group event AND distribution rule ("Dropping either is a different, weaker claim"); settle is distributive (each body and each marker comes to rest separately), so both rules are missing.

defect_summary: The compliant form adds, beside each group event, (Implication (PartOf $x sk_bodies_1) (And (Member (sk_settle $x) settle) (Patient (sk_settle $x) $x) (Location (sk_settle $x) sk_bottom_1) (Past (sk_settle $x)))) (STV 1.0 0.9) and its sk_markers_1 twin - the full conclusion bundle including the Location oblique and Past, as the Both-dogs-barked pattern shows, not the reduced form the reviewer wrote.
notes: The Patient-vs-Theme call on the settling groups is genuinely borderline (a mass moved by gravity takes Patient, un-powered relocation of dropped things takes Theme), but Patient is explicitly licensed, so it is not a defect.
